steps.question: Do the counts.csv (12000 genes x 6 samples) and metadata.csv (6 samples x condition) align correctly on sample IDs, and are library sizes / PCA consistent with the stated 3 treated vs 3 control unpaired design with no outlier samples?
constraints: Use the raw integer counts.csv exactly as provided (STAR+featureCounts output) — no upstream TPM/RPKM conversion
Treat 'gene symbol' as the row identifier from the first column of counts.csv
acceptance_criteria: Sample columns in counts.csv are confirmed to match rows in metadata.csv (same 6 sample IDs, same order or explicitly reordered)
Condition column recoded/verified as a two-level factor (treated vs control) with reference level = control
Library size (total counts per sample) and PCA on variance-stabilized/log-CPM data reported for all 6 samples
Any sample identified as a potential outlier (extreme library size or PCA separation not aligned with condition) is flagged explicitly, not silently dropped

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: With only 3 vs 3 replicates, statistical power is limited; genes with borderline padj should be reported with their exact padj, not rounded into a binary call
Do not report DE genes on raw p-value alone — padj (BH-adjusted) is the primary criterion given ~12000 tests
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=3) and control (n=3) liver samples, using a negative-binomial model on raw STAR/featureCounts integer counts?
constraints: Design formula must be ~ condition only (single batch, unpaired, no covariates available in metadata)
Report both the raw DESeq2 result and the shrunken log2FC — do not discard the unshrunken stat/pvalue
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 DataSet built from raw integer counts with design ~ condition, condition releveled so control is the reference
Default DESeq2 independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction applied; results table reports baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for every tested gene
apeglm (or ashr as fallback if apeglm fails to converge for any gene) used for log2FoldChange shrinkage, reported alongside unshrunken estimates
Full annotated DE table (gene symbol, log2FC, shrunken log2FC, padj) exported, plus explicit counts of genes at padj<0.05 and padj<0.1
MA plot and volcano plot generated from the shrunken estimates

steps.name: Pathway/functional enrichment of DE genes
caveats: Small n=3/3 design means the ranked gene list can be noisy; treat enrichment as hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory
GO-BP terms are nested and highly redundant — do not report raw term counts as if each were independent evidence
steps.question: Which biological pathways and processes are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
constraints: Use only the human-organism gene sets (WikiPathways human GMT, MSigDB Hallmark human GMT, MSigDB GO-BP human GMT, Reactome GMT filtered to Homo sapiens) — do not substitute mouse/rat sets
Gene identifiers in counts.csv are gene symbols; match directly against the HGNC-symbol GMT files without an ID-mapping step
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run against human WikiPathways, MSigDB Hallmark, MSigDB GO Biological Process, and Reactome gene sets (all confirmed present for Homo sapiens in the reference store)
Both an over-representation analysis on the significant gene list (padj<0.05) and a ranked GSEA on the full gene list (ranked by shrunken log2FC or DESeq2 stat) are reported
Results reported with BH-adjusted enrichment p-values, and GO-BP results explicitly flagged for parent/child term redundancy given the hierarchy
If fewer than ~10 genes pass padj<0.05, this is reported explicitly and GSEA on the full ranked list is treated as the primary result

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DESeq2 DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is raw integer gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples: 3 treated, 3 control liver samples) produced by STAR + featureCounts, with a simple unpaired, single-batch design. This is exactly the setting DESeq2's standard workflow is built for — it models raw counts directly with a negative binomial GLM and its own size-factor normalization, so no upstream TPM/CPM normalization from a transcript quantifier is needed or appropriate. The plan therefore: (1) loads counts + metadata, verifies sample-column/metadata alignment and condition coding, and performs basic QC (library size, PCA) to catch outliers/mislabeling before testing; (2) runs DESeq2 with the treated-vs-control contrast, using apeglm shrinkage for stable log2FC estimates and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control appropriate for a 12000-gene test; (3) produces a diagnostic MA/volcano/PCA report and the full annotated DE gene table; (4) takes the significant DE gene list into functional enrichment against human WikiPathways, MSigDB Hallmark, GO-BP, and Reactome gene sets (all confirmed present for Homo sapiens in the reference store) to interpret which biological processes are perturbed by treatment in liver. Sample size (n=3/group) is small — the QC step and enrichment step both carry explicit caveats about power and about not over-interpreting a handful of leading genes.
